clinical.citation: Identification of a novel LATS1 variant associated with familial cerebral cavernous malformations in a Chinese family (PMID: 35986120)

phenotypes: Familial cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) on MRI
Five-generation Chinese Han family with nine members affected
No CCM1-3 variants detected

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Identified by WES after exclusion of CCM1-3 variants. Co-segregated with the CCM phenotype in the family (Sanger sequencing). Predicted damaging in silico. Impaired angiogenesis in HUVEC assays supported a functional effect.

model_organism.citation: Hippo pathway links adipocyte plasticity to adipose tissue fibrosis (PMID: 36229481)
phenotypes: Lats1/2-knockout adipocytes dedifferentiated into DPP4+ progenitor cells
Lats1/2-knockout adipocytes converted to DPP4- myofibroblasts upon TGFβ stimulation
Hippo pathway inhibition impaired adipocyte identity and promoted ECM remodeling
Adipose tissue fibrosis, which was relieved by YAP/TAZ inhibition in obese mice with improved metabolic homeostasis

model_organism.citation: Hippo-Yap Signaling Maintains Sinoatrial Node Homeostasis (PMID: 36317529)
phenotypes: Lats1/2 inactivation in the cardiac conduction system (Hcn4CreERT2) caused severe sinus node dysfunction
Dysregulated calcium handling
Increased SAN fibrosis
Decreased Ryr2 expression
Increased Tgfb1 and Tgfb3 expression
Phenotype rescued by Yap/Taz deletion, with normal sinus rhythm and reduced fibrosis

model_organism.citation: YAP-Induced Glycolysis Drives Fibroinflammation and Disrupts Fibroblast Fidelity (PMID: 41165345)
phenotypes: Lats1/2 inactivation in cardiac fibroblasts activated glycolysis and drove fibroinflammation and fibrosis
Increased fibroblast proliferation
Fibroblasts shifted to a SOX9+ osteochondroprogenitor state
CSF1-mediated macrophage expansion
Macrophage IGF1 signaling enhanced fibroblast proliferation
Fibrosis reduced by glycolysis inhibition or blocking macrophage expansion

model_organism.citation: YAP/TAZ-CDC42 signaling regulates vascular tip cell migration (PMID: 28973878)
phenotypes: Endothelial Lats1/2 deletion caused nuclear YAP/TAZ translocation
Blocked endothelial migration during retinal angiogenesis
Phenocopied Yap/Taz-deficient mutants

model_organism.citation: Wnt and Src signals converge on YAP-TEAD to drive intestinal regeneration (PMID: 33950519)
phenotypes: Lats1/2 conditional knockout (YAP gain of activity) was sufficient to drive crypt hyperproliferation in the intestine

biological.citation: Regulation of the Hippo-YAP pathway by G-protein-coupled receptor signaling (PMID: 22863277)
biological.summary: LPA and S1P act through G12/13-coupled receptors to inhibit the Hippo kinases Lats1/2, which activates YAP/TAZ. Gs-coupled receptor stimulation by glucagon or epinephrine instead activates Lats1/2 kinase activity and inhibits YAP. This places LATS1/2 downstream of GPCR signaling.

biological.citation: Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation of DDR1 Counteracts the Hippo Pathway to Orchestrate Arterial Stiffening (PMID: 36475898)
biological.summary: DDR1 undergoes stiffness/collagen-induced liquid-liquid phase separation and co-condenses with LATS1 through its C-terminus. This competitively blocks MOB1 binding to LATS1 and prevents LATS1 phosphorylation, inactivating LATS1 and activating YAP. In mice, LATS1 inhibition reactivated YAP in Ddr1-deficient vessels and abrogated the arterial softening.

biological.citation: The Hippo pathway mediates Semaphorin signaling (PMID: 35613278)
biological.summary: Class 3 Semaphorins activate the core Hippo kinases LATS1/2 through PlexinA and p190RhoGAP. This suppresses lung cancer cell growth (SEMA3B restoration) and inhibits angiogenesis.

biological.citation: RIPK4 promotes epidermal differentiation through phase separation and activation of LATS1/2 (PMID: 40570855)
biological.summary: A kinome library screen identified RIPK4 as an alternative upstream kinase of LATS1/2. RIPK4 recruits LATS1/2 into liquid condensates and directly phosphorylates them. Ripk4 knockout mice show Yap/Taz activation in the epidermal granular layer, and disease-derived RIPK4 mutants fail to activate LATS1/2.

biological.citation: LATS1/2 loss promote tumor immune evasion in endometrial cancer through downregulating MHC-I expression (PMID: 38383447)
biological.summary: LATS1/2 are frequently mutated and downregulated in endometrial cancer. In CRISPR knockout cells, LATS1/2 loss lowered MHC-I independently of YAP. LATS1/2 directly bind and phosphorylate STAT1 at Ser727, promoting its nuclear accumulation and IRF1/NLRC5-driven MHC-I transcription, so loss of LATS1/2 confers resistance to immune-cell killing.
biological.sample_size: TCGA cohort plus in-house EC sample cohort

biological.citation: Methylation-associated inactivation of LATS1 and its effect on demethylation or overexpression on YAP and cell biological function in human renal cell carcinoma (PMID: 25270913)
biological.summary: LATS1 expression is reduced in RCC tissue (46.7% positive vs 76.7% in normal kidney) and correlates with grade and stage. The promoter is hypermethylated (97.5%) in 786-O cells. 5-Aza demethylation or LATS1 overexpression restored LATS1, reduced YAP, inhibited proliferation, and induced apoptosis and G1 arrest.

biological.citation: Lats1/2 Sustain Intestinal Stem Cells and Wnt Activation through TEAD-Dependent and Independent Transcription (PMID: 32259481)
biological.summary: In mouse intestine, Lats1/2 deletion causes loss of intestinal stem cells and Wnt-uncoupled crypt expansion. The Wnt inhibition is YAP/TAZ dependent but TEAD independent, because nuclear YAP/TAZ interact with TLE to block TCF-mediated transcription.

biological.citation: Hippo-Yap Signaling Maintains Sinoatrial Node Homeostasis (PMID: 36317529)
biological.summary: Conditional Lats1/2 inactivation in the sinoatrial node (Hcn4CreERT2) caused severe sinus node dysfunction, disrupted calcium handling with reduced Ryr2, and increased fibrosis with higher Tgfb1/3. Deleting Yap/Taz rescued the phenotype, so Lats1/2 act through Yap/Taz.

biological.citation: Expression of LATS1 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and its effect on tumor cell proliferation and invasion (PMID: 36029506)
biological.summary: LATS1 protein expression fell from 59.3% in normal epithelium to 11.3% in HNSCC on tissue microarray. LATS1 overexpression in B88 cells inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion and EMT, consistent with tumor suppressor activity.

biological.citation: LATS1-Beclin1 mediates a non-canonical connection between the Hippo pathway and autophagy (PMID: 32944618)
biological.summary: LATS1, but not LATS2, regulates sorafenib-induced lethal autophagy in HCC independently of its kinase activity, through a LATS1-specific domain. This is coupled to K27-linked ubiquitination and self-dimerization of Beclin-1 (BECN1).
